_comment: Hosts that stopped answering automated fetches AFTER content citing them was written and
verified. A host belongs here only when a human has decided to keep the pages that cite it.
verify_place_sources.py reports their assertions as UNCHECKED rather than failing the run, and
prints the block on every run so it cannot quietly become permanent. --strict re-fails them.
This file never reaches a reader. No page renders source status, because a source we cannot
re-fetch is not evidence that a price is wrong, and a warning on the page would tell a traveler
to distrust copy that nothing has contradicted.
Do NOT add a host here to make a new page publishable. A source that never verified is not a
blocked source, it is an unsourced claim, and the attraction does not get a page.
EXHAUST THE PIPELINE BEFORE ADDING ANYTHING HERE. royalcollection.org.uk was listed here for
about an hour on 2026-08-15, after every path on it and its rct.uk alias returned 403 and two
live pages were nearly retired over it. It was not blocked. It serves a page and then refuses
the next request seconds later, indefinitely, and the fixed 1.5s per-host gap could not satisfy
it. Adaptive per-host backoff made all six assertions pass on a cold run. The entry was deleted,
because an excuse that outlives its cause is how a fixable fault becomes permanent.
